title: Ends supply open distinctions that the knot test cannot tell from loops
claim: On a connected, locally finite, infinite graph, for any charge: (1) a parity of finitely many edge variables of the Tseitin system is constant exactly when its support is a finite cut with a finite side; otherwise it is open either because a finite circuit meets it oddly (loop-supplied, changed by a finite change of solution) or because it is a finite cut with infinitely many vertices on both sides (end-supplied, unchanged by every change in the closure of the finite cycle space); finite graphs have only the first kind. (2) A vertex relation passes K1-K3 exactly when no nonempty proper subset of its edges has constant parity; at degree 3 exactly when its edges are open, so the 3-regular tree carries a knot at every vertex, all of whose openness is end-supplied, and a finite tree carries none. (3) Adding one edge outside any finite ball across an end-supplied cut keeps the ball's projection and makes the parity loop-supplied, so no finite part and no K1-K3 verdict decides the source. (4) For each end, the uniform measure on the solutions whose hole went to that end has the moments of the tangle pseudo-expectation of SOS-SIZE-20261020-001B-P001 Theorem 1, for every finite F; on one-ended graphs this is the uniform measure on all solutions. (5) A computable binary tree with root charge 1 has a satisfiable system and no computable solution.
failure_conditions: On a declared graph and charge, a parity's computed constancy or value disagrees with its loop/end/fixed classification, or the open truncation's projection changes with the radius.
A closed finite truncation has an open parity that no finite circuit supplies.
A knotlab K1-K3 verdict on a projected vertex relation disagrees with the classification's prediction, a vertex of the 3-regular tree fails to be a knot, or a closed finite tree carries a knot.
A fold pair or a one-edge modification outside the ball changes the ball's projection, or leaves the parity end-supplied.
A computed moment differs from the tangle formula for the graph's end (one-ended) or for the chosen end (conditioned), or an end-separating cut has a nonzero unconditioned moment.
A control (end parities called constant, closed tree with the infinite prediction, edge inside the ball, edge on one side, infinite side's charge, wrong end, free edge at a dead end) is accepted.
A published statement of Theorem 3 or Theorem 4 is found (novelty only).
foundation_claim_scope: K1-K3 verdicts on projections of Tseitin systems on infinite graphs, and where their open distinctions come from. No native recurrence, composed topology, path, metric, space or physical claim.

validation.status: checked: prose proof; check.py computes exact GF(2) projections of open truncations on nine infinite graphs (stable in the radius), classifies every parity of the edges near the root from closed truncations, runs knotlab's K1-K3 check on 28 vertex relations and a closed-tree control, verifies fold pairs and 152 one-edge modifications, compares 65,536 grid moments and four end-conditioned moment tables with the tangle formula, and samples a finite shadow of Proposition 5; seven controls rejected; no human or external review
validation.level: V1 prose proof with executable checks; cites Diestel-Kuhn (2004), Bruhn-Stein (2007), Berger-Bruhn (2011), Diestel (2017), Grigoriev (2001), Kleene (1952) and SOS-SIZE-20261020-001B-P001; no trusted kernel.
validation.novelty: candidate-local-delta. A search on 2026-10-20 found the topological cycle space and its end-parity characterization (Diestel-Kuhn; Bruhn-Stein; Berger-Bruhn), ends as tangles (Diestel), and no treatment of Tseitin formulas on infinite graphs, of the source of openness, or of the tangle pseudo-expectation as a measure at an end. Lemma 2, Theorem 1 and Proposition 2 restate classical results; Theorems 2-4 are short consequences; Proposition 5 is folklore-level.
validation.independence: Written by Claude in one session at the repository owner's request on 2026-10-20.
